title: A Vector for the Colony
premise: Rafael Reyes, an insurance investigator cataloguing the 'impossible accidents' of the dying colony Meridian, discovers the accidents are cover for a covert weapons program — and that a nine-second gravity flicker across the system was its test firing. Branded a witness to a war crime, Rafael joins a ragtag crew of colonists, defectors, and one amnesiac engineer who may have built the weapon, carrying proof of it toward the neutral relay station where peace talks hang by a thread. Hunted by corporate enforcers and their own government, they must choose between delivering the message that exposes the program — risking open war — or burying it and letting the colony's slow death continue. In the end, Rafael broadcasts the truth not to the negotiators but to every citizen at once, forcing justice outside any courtroom, while the amnesiac engineer recovers her memory and chooses to stand trial beside them.
about_author: Ulyana Whitlock is a former maritime claims adjuster who spent eleven years investigating losses at sea before turning to fiction, a career she credits for her obsession with paperwork as evidence of human folly. She writes from a converted lighthouse keeper's cottage on the Atlantic coast, where she lives with her partner and an ill-tempered rescue cat named Actuary.

chapters.title: The Arithmetic of Falling Things
chapters.summary: Rafael Reyes, POV. Investigating a crane collapse on dying colony Meridian, Rafael notices the third 'accident' this quarter shares an impossible signature: structural stress patterns that don't match any known cause. The emotional beat is quiet dread — the colony is failing, and someone is hiding why. Establishes Rafael's meticulous voice and loneliness.

chapters.title: Nine Seconds
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV. Gravity flickers across the entire system for exactly nine seconds; birds fall, rivers lift, and Rafael's apartment ceiling rains dust. When it ends, comms are jammed and the colonial governor declares a routine anomaly. Rafael files the event in their log — and finds a prior record of an identical flicker, redacted. Beat: vertigo and suspicion.

chapters.title: The Widow Who Kept Receipts
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV. A widow of one 'accident' victim hires Rafael privately, handing over her husband's hidden data chips. The chips point to the deep-shield facility Kestrel Station and a project called VECTOR. That night, Rafael's office is ransacked. Beat: grief transmuted into purpose; Rafael accepts they're no longer just an observer.

chapters.title: Crew of the Long Odds
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV, introducing the crew: smuggler-pilot Odile Voss, ex-medic Tam, and teenage stowaway Juno who hacks doors for fun. Rafael buys passage off-world with the widow's money, carrying the chips. Beat: wary found-family formation — strangers bound by distrust of the same institutions.

chapters.title: The Woman Without a Yesterday
chapters.summary: Engineer Sefa Idris's POV. Found drifting in a lifepod near Kestrel with total amnesia, Sefa carries muscle memory of the station's systems and a tattooed serial number matching VECTOR documentation. The crew debates abandoning her; Juno votes to keep her. Beat: fragile trust; Sefa fears what her own hands might remember.

chapters.title: Paper Trails and Burn Wards
chapters.summary: Tam's POV. Treating refugees from a mining platform 'decommissioned' after the first flicker, Tam recognizes radiation burns inconsistent with official reports. The crew realizes the flicker wasn't a test failure — it was a successful strike on a target no one will name. Beat: moral horror hardening into resolve.

chapters.title: Kestrel Station, Unlit
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. The crew infiltrates abandoned sections of Kestrel Station, dodging corporate security drones. They find VECTOR's launch bay: a gravity-manipulation array capable of crushing cities or cracking moons. Sefa's body reacts to the controls before her mind does. Beat: awe curdling into terror at what humanity built here.

chapters.title: What Her Hands Remember
chapters.summary: Sefa's POV. Under pressure from a security sweep, Sefa instinctively reroutes power and saves the crew — proving she helped build the array. Fragments return: a supervisor's voice, a countdown, her own signature on a safety waiver she was coerced into signing. Beat: shame and self-estrangement; she asks Rafael to promise she'll face judgment.

chapters.title: The Message
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV. Assembled evidence — chips, burn records, Sefa's fragments — forms a message: VECTOR is operational, tested on civilian targets, and scheduled for full deployment within weeks unless exposed at the neutral peace talks on Relay Concord. The crew must decide who carries it. Beat: the weight of witness; Rafael volunteers.

chapters.title: Hunted Through the Shallows
chapters.summary: Juno's POV. A chase through asteroid shoals as corporate hunter ships corner the Long Odds. Juno's improvised ECM tricks and Odile's reckless flying buy escape at the cost of their fuel reserves and Tam's injured arm. Beat: found family forged under fire; Juno stops being a stowaway and becomes crew.

chapters.title: Terms of Surrender
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV. A colonial marshal offers amnesty: hand over the evidence and Sefa, and everyone walks free. Rafael refuses, learning the marshal's own family died in the 'decommissioned' mine — even the law's servants are victims. Beat: temptation and refusal; justice outside the law crystallizes as the crew's creed.

chapters.title: The Quiet Between Stars
chapters.summary: Sefa's POV. Drifting on minimal power, the crew rests. Sefa and Rafael share watch; she confesses her fear that recovering her memory will make her unforgivable. Rafael tells her memory isn't guilt — it's testimony. Beat: tenderness and intimacy; the theme of memory reframed as moral duty rather than burden.

chapters.title: Concord Under Lockdown
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. Relay Concord, site of the peace talks, is sealed under pretext of a security threat — actually VECTOR's sponsors preparing a false-flag incident to collapse negotiations. The crew slips in among refugee traffic. Beat: claustrophobic tension; the clock is now measured in hours.

chapters.title: Diplomats and Butchers
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV. Rafael contacts a weary mediator, Ambassador Chen, who believes the evidence but lacks authority to act without triggering war accusations. Chen reveals VECTOR's deployment order is signed and countersigned — by officials on both sides of the war. Beat: disillusionment; the enemy is not one nation but a machine spanning all of them.

chapters.title: Sefa Remembers Everything
chapters.summary: Sefa's POV. Confronting the array's control interface aboard Concord's captured relay core, Sefa's memory returns fully: she designed the failsafe that could disable VECTOR permanently — and she erased her own memory to hide it from her handlers. Beat: catharsis and terror; the key to everything was inside her all along.

chapters.title: The False Flag
chapters.summary: Tam's POV. VECTOR's operators trigger a staged attack on Concord to blame the opposing faction. Tam and Juno sabotage the staging site, exposing the operation's fingerprints, but Tam is captured covering Juno's escape. Beat: sacrifice; the cost of truth becomes personal and irreversible.

chapters.title: Ninety-Six Hours
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV. With Tam imprisoned and VECTOR's full deployment imminent, the crew has under four days. Legal channels are dead — Chen warns any formal accusation will be buried. Rafael proposes the unthinkable: broadcast everything directly to every citizen in the system, bypassing courts, governments, and armies alike. Beat: desperate audacity.

chapters.title: Storming the Relay
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. The crew assaults Concord's primary broadcast spire — Odile flying, Juno hacking, Rafael carrying the evidence core, Sefa navigating systems only she understands. They free Tam mid-assault. Beat: kinetic climax building; every member's arc converges on one act of collective courage.

chapters.title: Broadcast
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV. On the spire, Rafael transmits the full VECTOR record — the tests, the burns, the signatures — to every screen and speaker in the system, then surrenders the spire rather than destroy it. Citizens on both sides see the same truth simultaneously. Beat: the climax's moral peak; justice delivered not by verdict but by witness.

chapters.title: Gravity Holds
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs interwoven. VECTOR's operators attempt a final firing; Sefa activates her buried failsafe, killing the array forever as soldiers on both sides refuse illegal orders in the broadcast's wake. The flicker never comes. Beat: release — the held breath of an entire system finally exhaling.

chapters.title: Testimony
chapters.summary: Sefa's POV. Months later, tribunals convene — imperfect, political, but real. Sefa testifies to her own complicity and stands trial; Rafael testifies as investigator, not defendant. Tam heals, Juno starts school, Odile refits the Long Odds. Beat: bittersweet accountability; justice is slow, but it belongs to everyone now.

chapters.title: A Vector for the Colony
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV. Rafael returns to Meridian, delivering the widow her husband's vindicated file and watching supply ships arrive for a colony that will live after all. Closing the impossible-accidents log, Rafael opens a new notebook titled simply 'Witnesses.' Beat: quiet hope; memory kept is a promise kept, and found family endures.
